heading: Thoughtful websites.
intro: I design and build websites for businesses—pairing a clear purpose with a visual identity that feels like you.
seoTitle: Tedits Studio — Thoughtful web design, Zambia & worldwide
seoDescription: Tedits Studio creates considered websites with colour palettes and designs tailored to your brand. Independent web design based in Zambia, available for remote projects worldwide.

title: Olive & Ember
description: A warm, editorial catering website that brings occasions, sample menus, and an enquiry journey together.
idea: Good food can make a big celebration feel special and an ordinary week feel easier. I imagined a catering business that cared about both, with a website that felt as welcoming as sitting down at its table.
execution: Warm greens, generous food photography, and an unhurried layout set that feeling. Sample menus give visitors something to picture, while the enquiry flow starts with the occasion they have in mind.
disclaimer: Demo project for a fictional business. No client commission, testimonials, or business results are claimed. Stock photos illustrate the concept.

title: Rivet & Beam
description: An industrial website concept with a clear material catalogue and a flexible enquiry flow for standard supplies or custom fabrication.
idea: Some people know the exact steel section they need. Others have a rough sketch and an idea they want to make real. This concept gives both a comfortable starting point, without expecting everyone to speak the language of fabrication.
execution: The material catalogue offers a straightforward route for familiar jobs. For everything else, there is room to describe an idea, add a drawing, and work through the details in an enquiry preview.
disclaimer: Fictional business and independent concept. No real company commissioned, approved, or endorsed this project. Photography is illustrative; the demo sends nothing.

title: AFTERHOURS
description: A record-sleeve-inspired studio concept with an interactive vinyl record and two instrumental listening previews produced by TeddyBear.
idea: The starting point was the feeling of making music after the rest of the world has gone quiet. I wanted a place where someone could settle in, put a track on, and get a sense of the person behind the sound.
execution: Warm amber, dark surfaces, and a spinning record bring that late-night mood into the page. The tracks stay close at hand, so listening feels like the natural next step.
disclaimer: Fictional studio and independent design concept. The featured instrumentals were produced by TeddyBear; The Lead includes an R&B sample. Licence cards are illustrative and offer no music rights or prices. No client results are claimed.

title: Little Joy Play Co.
description: A soft-play hire website with a gentle, playful feel, room for photographs and a simple way to plan a celebration.
scope: Visual design · Responsive development · Interaction design
idea: I imagined Little Joy as a welcoming place for parents to plan a celebration. I started with the things I’d want to know: what the play area looks like, what’s included and whether it will fit.
execution: I borrowed the rounded shapes of soft-play equipment and paired them with gentle colours and generous photographs. Initially, I put everything on one long page, then gave each part its own space. I wanted parents to get a feel for Little Joy first and explore the details at their own pace.
disclaimer: I created Little Joy as an independent concept for a fictional business, with stock photography to help tell the story. The prices and packages are examples, and the enquiry form is a preview: nothing is sent or booked.

title: Tedeats Events
description: An invitation-inspired events concept with photographs emerging from an envelope and a bouquet tracing the planning journey.
idea: A physical invitation makes an occasion feel real before anyone arrives. I used that first gesture to imagine Tedeats Events: a fictional planning and hosting brand where the website itself extends the invitation.
execution: Cherry red, paper white and editorial type set the tone. Photographs emerge from an envelope and settle into a stack as you scroll. A bouquet follows a curved route through the planning stages, with slower photographic layers giving the journey depth.
disclaimer: Tedeats Events is a fictional brand and independent portfolio concept. AI-generated imagery illustrates imagined events. The enquiry form is a local demonstration: nothing is sent, booked or paid for. No client commission, testimonials or business results are claimed.
